title: Two Counts for One Clone — Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria Budd-Chiari Thrombosis (H030), RBC Hemolysis/Transfusion Dilution vs. Granulocyte FLAER/CD157 Flow Cytometry

teenKit.tldr: A patient's blood test reveals an impossible mystery: 99% of his white blood cells carry a dangerous genetic mutation, but only 5% of his red blood cells show it. The secret lies in how different cells live, die, and get replaced inside the human body.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how the body masks deadly genetic mutations in blood cells teaches us how to read medical data without being fooled by biological smoke and mirrors.
keyTakeaways: All blood cells originate from the exact same stem cell factory in the bone marrow, meaning their genetic mutation rates should theoretically match.
Red blood cells carrying the mutation are aggressively destroyed by the immune system (hemolysis) and constantly diluted by medical blood transfusions, shrinking their visible numbers.
White blood cells like granulocytes live much shorter lives and aren't replaced by transfusions, making them accurate witnesses of the true, massive size of the mutant cell clone.

vocab.meaning: A rare, life-threatening blood disease where red blood cells lose their protective surface shields and get brutally destroyed by the body's own immune system.
A high-tech laboratory laser machine that counts and analyzes millions of individual cells in a liquid sample at blazing-fast speeds.
A logical error where you only look at the survivors that made it through a filter, completely missing the ones that were destroyed or filtered out.
A fluorescent chemical probe that sticks to specific anchor molecules on cells, acting like a molecular spotlight to expose genetic defects.

quiz.question: If white blood cells and red blood cells come from the exact same stem cell factory, why did the patient's lab results show such a massive percentage difference?
options: The laboratory equipment was completely broken and miscalculated both counts.
Red blood cells were destroyed by the disease and diluted by medical transfusions, while white blood cells were not.
The patient's bone marrow suddenly stopped producing red blood cells entirely.
White blood cells reproduce much faster than red blood cells can mutate.
quiz.explanation: Mutant red blood cells were rapidly killed off and replaced with donor blood from transfusions, hiding the true size of the mutation that was still fully visible in the white blood cells.

quiz.question: What is the primary job of a technique like flow cytometry in a case like this?
options: To physically separate healthy organs from diseased organs during surgery
To rapidly measure thousands of individual cells using lasers to see which ones possess or lack specific surface proteins
To inject synthetic stem cells directly into the patient's bone marrow
To filter out dangerous toxins from the patient's plasma before it reaches the liver
quiz.explanation: Flow cytometry uses lasers and fluorescent tags to rapidly screen individual cells, revealing exactly which ones are missing their protective surface anchors.

quiz.question: Why do doctors look at white blood cells (like granulocytes) instead of red blood cells to find the true size of a PNH clone?
options: White blood cells are immune to all known genetic mutations.
White blood cells are never affected by blood transfusions and reflect the true bone marrow output.
Red blood cells are too large for laboratory machines to analyze properly.
White blood cells live for decades, recording every change in the body.
quiz.explanation: Because white blood cells aren't replaced by transfusions and have predictable lifespans, they give an honest, unmasked look at what the bone marrow is actually churning out.
